_readme: Chapters and deck text shown on the site. Edit freely. Decklists come from ydk/<slug>.ydk; card counts, the type breakdown and hand odds are calculated by the build. 'updated' is set automatically when a deck's .ydk changes.

collections.title: Method
collections.family: Method — decks that each showcase a summoning method.
collections.intro: Five decks covering all six summoning methods — Synchro, Xyz, Ritual, Link, Fusion and Pendulum — each built to showcase its method.

decks.name: White Forest / Diabellstar
decks.tagline: A LIGHT Spellcaster Synchro engine fused with the Diabellstar / Sinful Spoils package and a Super Polymerization removal suite.

decks.name: Horus Mitsurugi
decks.tagline: A Horus Level 8 graveyard-revival engine braided into the Mitsurugi DARK Reptile Ritual line, sharing a Rank 8 Xyz toolbox.

decks.name: Kashtira Maliss
decks.tagline: A Maliss DARK Cyberse banish-loop combo through the Link Monster line, backed by Bystials and an empty-field Kashtira package.

decks.name: Runick Typhoon
decks.tagline: A Runick Quick-Play mill / control shell locked behind Inspector Boarder and Dimensional Fissure, closing with Radiant Typhoon Fonix and TY-PHON.

decks.name: Ryu-Ge Mitsurugi
decks.tagline: A Level 10 Pendulum / Realm control shell fused with the Mitsurugi Ritual line, climbing a Rank 10–12 Xyz and Synchro toolbox.

collections.title: Playstyle Pt. 1
collections.family: Playstyle — decks that each play the game their own way. Part 1 is how a deck controls the game; Part 2 is how it closes it.
collections.intro: Four decks defined by how they control the game — Defense-Position Battle Phase dominance, a Synchro grind, tempo control going first, and tempo control going second.

decks.name: Scareclaw Kashtira
decks.tagline: Defense-Position beatdown and OTK built around Scareclaw's self-Summon chain, with a Kashtira disruption package and Visas Starfrost as the glue.

decks.name: Earthbound Resonator
decks.tagline: A DARK Dragon Synchro grind deck built on the Resonator engine into the Red Dragon Archfiend family, with Earthbound Immortal Red Nova as a Level 12 shortcut.

decks.name: Primite Blue-Eyes
decks.tagline: The classic Blue-Eyes White Dragon Synchro / Fusion control shell, reinforced with the Primite Normal-Monster sub-engine for extra consistency.

decks.name: Swordsoul Tenyi
decks.tagline: A Wyrm Synchro shell built on Swordsoul Tokens and the Tenyi non-Effect sub-engine, running one of the heaviest going-second suites in the collection.

collections.title: Playstyle Pt. 2
collections.family: Playstyle — decks that each play the game their own way. Part 1 is how a deck controls the game; Part 2 is how it closes it.
collections.intro: Three decks defined by how they close the game — swift Battle Phase OTKs, Synchro spam, and an unaffected Link tower.

decks.name: Tenpai Wyrm Striker
decks.tagline: A three-engine hybrid: Swordsoul Tokens and Tenyi build Wyrm Synchros on the Main Phase, then Tenpai / Sangen Synchro Summons FIRE Dragons mid-Battle Phase for the kill, backed by Sky Striker interaction.

decks.name: Synchron Adventurer
decks.tagline: The classic Synchron / Stardust Synchro combo engine, supplemented by an Adventurer Token sub-engine for a free body and a hard negate.

decks.name: Ignister
decks.tagline: A @Ignister Cyberse Link climb from Level 1–5 searchers into Dark Templar, Allied Code Talker, and Accesscode Talker, topped by The Arrival Cyberse @Ignister — a Link-6 tower unaffected by other cards' effects.

collections.title: Nostalgic Fun Pt. 1
collections.family: Nostalgic Fun — archetypes I love, rebuilt to hold up today.
collections.intro: Old favorites rebuilt with modern support — a Fusion toolbox, a low-LP floodgate deck, and a Trap-driven boss-monster shell.

decks.name: Branded Dracotail
decks.tagline: A Fusion toolbox built on Fallen of Albaz and Branded Fusion, reinforced by the Dracotail engine's Quick-Effect Fusions and on-material removal triggers.

decks.name: Dinomorphia Ryzeal
decks.tagline: A Trap-Fusion floodgate deck that scales its bosses off low Life Points, paired with a Ryzeal Rank 4 toolbox and a small Kashtira package.

decks.name: Metalmorph Fiendsmith
decks.tagline: A Max Metalmorph Trap toolbox running three boss monsters off Red-Eyes Dragons and Zoa, with the Fiendsmith LIGHT Fiend engine layered in for extension.

collections.title: Nostalgic Fun Pt. 2
collections.family: Nostalgic Fun — archetypes I love, rebuilt to hold up today.
collections.intro: Three throwbacks built on birds, wind and moonlight — a Blackwing Synchro combo, a Radiant Typhoon Quick-Play engine, and a Lunalight Fusion chain — with two of them sharing the Angelechy engine.

decks.name: Blackwing Angelechy
decks.tagline: The Blackwing DARK Synchro combo fused with the Angelechy LIGHT Fairy engine, whose Synchros sit face-up as Continuous Spells for extra utility.

decks.name: Radiant Typhoon Angelechy
decks.tagline: A Radiant Typhoon WIND Quick-Play / MST engine layered with Angelechy Synchro placement and a Fallen of Albaz Fusion package.
keyCards: Radiant Typhoon Fonix, the Great Flame

decks.name: Lunalight
decks.tagline: The Lunalight DARK Beast-Warrior Fusion engine running the full Dancer chain, from Cat Dancer up to Liger Dancer, backed by a deep hand-trap suite.

collections.title: Nostalgic Fun Pt. 3
collections.family: Nostalgic Fun — archetypes I love, rebuilt to hold up today.
collections.intro: Two decks that each define a format in their own way — a Level 2 toolbox engine and a floodgate control shell built around one enormous beater.

decks.name: Spright Dogmatika
decks.tagline: The Spright Level / Rank / Link 2 engine paired with the Dogmatika Extra-Deck-send package, running one of the heaviest hand-trap suites in the collection.

decks.name: Gren Maju Da Eiza
decks.tagline: A floodgate control shell stacking Macro Cosmos, Necrovalley, and Inspector Boarder, closing games with a Gren Maju Da Eiza whose attack grows with every banished card.
